review_output: {"summary":"Not ready. Migration 115 appears to close the prior-114 race only when the payment writer uses ReadCommitted. In ReadCommitted, the AFTER trigger's plpgsql INSERT…SELECT takes a fresh snapshot after the SHARE wait, so it should see the relinked order. Under RepeatableRead the race comes back. Under Serializable it depends on SSI, which has not been checked. The SHARE lock can also cause new deadlocks, and one case depends on a foreign key that wasn't supplied. The tests only cover ReadCommitted, and the synchronized20 Serializable gate is still failing or unchecked.","findings":[{"severity":"BLOCKER","area":"RepeatableRead/Serializable snapshot after lock wait","file":"prisma/migrations/20261016030000_live_metric_order_payment_serialization/migration.sql","issue":"FOR SHARE makes the payment UPDATE wait for the relink, but it doesn't change which data the payment trigger can see.","evidence":"Relink runs first and holds SHARE on P. Payment tx T2 (RepeatableRead) has a snapshot from before the relink commit. Its UPDATE waits; P was only locked, not modified, so no 40001 is raised. Then the 010000 AFTER trigger at L35-38 reads CommerceOrder from T2's old snapshot and finds the old link.","impact":"The relink's new-window event commits before T2. T2 then commits its metadata change with no new-window event, which is the original 114 race. Serializable only catches this if SSI finds both rw-conflicts, and only if the peer transaction is also Serializable.","recommended_fix":"Give the order trigger a write conflict instead of a SHARE lock, for example by updating a per-payment link-fence row. The payment trigger should lock or update the same row so RepeatableRead/Serializable writers get 40001 and retry. Alternatively, fail closed when not in ReadCommitted.","required_test":"Run the link-race script with both writers at RepeatableRead and at Serializable, plus mixed isolation levels. Expect either a 40001 retry or a new-window event committed after the payment.","confidence":0.75},{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"Deadlock/liveness","file":"prisma/migrations/20261016030000_live_metric_order_payment_serialization/migration.sql","issue":"Lock order changes from order row then payment row to the reverse in other flows.","evidence":"The BEFORE ROW trigger runs after the order tuple is locked and then requests SHARE on P (L14-17). A payment flow that runs UPDATE payment and then UPDATE order holds P and waits for O, while a link/create flow holds O and waits for P. A foreign key's KEY SHARE did not conflict with NO KEY UPDATE before this change.","impact":"New 40P01 deadlocks and 40001 errors in checkout and webhook paths. The tests only cover lock_timeout.","recommended_fix":"Take payment locks before order locks in every service path. Add bounded retry for 40P01/40001 in the synchronized gate.","required_test":"Two transactions with crossed payment→order and order→payment order. Assert one gets 40P01, the retry succeeds, and the ledger is complete.","confidence":0.7},{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"Missing dependency: payment insert vs pre-linked order","file":"prisma/migrations/20261016010000_live_metric_order_window_source/migration.sql","issue":"Correctness depends on a composite foreign key from CommerceOrder(primaryPaymentTransactionId, vendorId) to PaymentTransaction(id, vendorId). That key was not supplied.","evidence":"If an order can reference an uncommitted or missing payment, the lock at L14-17 locks nothing. The concurrent payment INSERT trigger (L35) doesn't see the uncommitted order, so the order event commits first and the payment commits with no event.","impact":"A stale proof is possible for the order's window.","recommended_fix":"Supply the foreign key definition and its ON DELETE behaviour, or add the key. If no key exists, take the fence for the payment id even when the row doesn't exist.","required_test":"Run a concurrent order INSERT with the link and a payment INSERT. Check the ledger for each commit order.","confidence":0.5},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Upgrade invalidation ordering","file":"prisma/migrations/20261016030000_live_metric_order_payment_serialization/migration.sql","issue":"The L32 bump does not drain in-flight payment transactions.","evidence":"CREATE TRIGGER locks only CommerceOrder. A payment tx that already read the old relation can commit after the migration bump, after a proof has been issued on the new revision.","impact":"A stale proof can survive the upgrade.","recommended_fix":"Run LOCK TABLE PaymentTransaction and CommerceOrder IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE before creating the trigger and bumping.","required_test":"Populated-upgrade test with an open payment tx during the migration (this test is still pending).","confidence":0.55},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Test sufficiency / RLS","file":"scripts/wp20-order-window-link-race.mjs","issue":"The test proves the follower was blocked, not that the result is correct. It also runs only at the default isolation level. Separately, the lock function doesn't set row_security=off.","evidence":"There is no isolationLevel option on the transactions at L24 and L36. The evidence scope says other schedules are still pending. If PaymentTransaction uses FORCE RLS, PERFORM can silently lock nothing.","impact":"The tests can pass while the RepeatableRead/Serializable, deadlock and insert holes remain open.","recommended_fix":"Parameterize the isolation level and add the insert and deadlock schedules. Set row_security=off on the lock function so it fails closed.","required_test":"Isolation-level matrix through the actual synchronized20 Serializable gate.","confidence":0.65}]}
